title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 369
paragraphs: To the Ionians and Carians who had helped him, Psammetichos granted portions of land to settle in, opposite one another with the river Nile between them; these were called the “Encampments.” These portions of land he gave them, and besides he paid them all he had promised. Moreover, he placed with them Egyptian boys to be taught the Greek language, and from these — who learned the language thoroughly — are descended the present class of interpreters in Egypt. The Ionians and Carians occupied these portions of land for a long time; they lay toward the sea, a little below the city of Bubastis, on what is called the Pelusian mouth of the Nile. King Amasis later removed these men from there and settled them at Memphis, making them into a bodyguard for himself against the Egyptians. And since they settled in Egypt, we who are Greeks know with certainty, through our dealings with them, everything that happened in Egypt from the reign of king Psammetichos onward; for these were the first men of foreign speech to settle in Egypt. In the land from which they were removed, there still remained down to my own time the sheds where their ships had been drawn up and the ruins of their houses.
